chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Hopping freights and joining the Civilian Conservation Corps
summary: Thompson had hopped trains as a boy, was not afraid to travel, and at 17-18 joined the CCC to escape, helped by his typing skill.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: And on several occasions I as a little boy before I had sort of had the inclinations, you know, as a boy in these neighborhoods where the freight trains are around, you know, we had had experience in hopping freight trains, you know, and getting away with it for short little jaunts of a few hundred yards, and so forth. So I wasn't really afraid to travel, and having seen these hobos, and the publicity of these hobos at that time was so great that there was some inclination to let me know that there were other ways of getting along in the world where I didn't have to stay necessarily where my family had anchored themselves with this christian background and this christian obligation, which I didn't consider mine.
Do you understand what I mean?

So in the process I went to the army because it was when they were having the Civilian Conservation Corps organized, which was a sort of a combination of the WPA organization people, which was the people who needed assistance. In fact previous to that I remember a couple of times just as a kid you know when you're around with other kids -- I don't know even know whether my father appreciated
it or not. I don't think he wanted me to do it, but I saw other people going down there and they used to give out food, you know, for poor people.

Well, I don't think my family was actually poor, because we had just about everything we needed, and then you know, I mean I think a minister has a little help from people that other people wouldn't have because they appreciate his help, and sometimes they do things in food that they couldn't do in salary.
Even if they didn't take up enough money to maybe pay his salary, he might get -- and they usually furnished us a very decent home.

But I went down with the rest of the people, and I remember getting some bacon or something like that, whatever they were giving away. But it wasn't in my family desirable for me to do that. But in other words -- but I took advantage of this situation, of the Civilian Conservation Corps enjoying the army, so that I could get away from the situation, get away from home.
I was exactly -- well I was 17 plus and by virtue of my turning 18 in a short time I was able to join. And also because of my ability to type. You know, there
was a need for clerical positions, and you know, people who could fill these clerical positions at the time.
